episodes.title: Uveitis Anatomy & the SUN Classification Explained
episodes.description:
What happens when a patient walks in with a red, painful eye — and the inflammation could be anywhere inside it? How do doctors even begin to describe, classify, and communicate what they're seeing? The answer lies in one of ophthalmology's most important frameworks: the SUN classification system.

In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down uveitis anatomy and the Standardization of Uveitis Nomenclature (SUN) working group's classification system in a way that's clear, engaging, and genuinely useful — whether you're a medical student, ophthalmology resident, optometrist, or simply curious about how the eye works.

We cover the three layers of the eye and what the uvea actually is, then walk through all four anatomical categories of uveitis: anterior uveitis, intermediate uveitis, posterior uveitis, and panuveitis. You'll learn what distinguishes each type, where the inflammation is located, what symptoms patients experience, and which conditions are commonly associated with each. We also explore how the SUN classification describes uveitis by onset, duration, and disease course — and why those descriptors matter just as much as anatomy when it comes to diagnosis and treatment.

Finally, we touch on how the SUN grading system for cells, flare, and vitreous haze makes clinical research more objective and reproducible — ultimately improving outcomes for patients worldwide.

Uveitis accounts for up to 15% of legal blindness in developed countries. Understanding how to classify it accurately isn't just academic — it's vision-saving.

Listen now and build a stronger foundation in uveitis. For more ophthalmology content, visit Focuslinks.in.

episodes.title: Anterior Uveitis: Cells & Flare at the Slit Lamp Explained
episodes.description:
Ever sat at the slit lamp and wondered what those tiny floating specks or that mysterious hazy glow in the anterior chamber actually mean? In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take a deep dive into one of the most essential clinical skills in ophthalmology — recognizing and grading cells and flare in anterior uveitis.

We break down exactly how the blood-aqueous barrier breaks down during inflammation, why white blood cells and proteins flood the anterior chamber, and how to set up your slit lamp beam for the clearest possible view. You will learn the SUN grading system for anterior chamber cells step by step, understand how flare is graded and what plastic aqueous really looks like, and discover why cells and flare do not always tell the same story — a distinction that can make or break your treatment decisions.

We also cover the key associated findings you cannot afford to miss: keratic precipitates including the classic mutton-fat KPs of granulomatous uveitis, posterior synechiae, iris bombé, and the very real risk of uveitis-related glaucoma. The episode wraps up with a real-world clinical scenario of HLA-B27 associated anterior uveitis that ties every concept together into a clear, practical management approach.

Whether you are a medical student, optometry trainee, ophthalmology resident, or a curious clinician brushing up on your fundamentals, this episode will sharpen the way you see and interpret the anterior chamber forever.

Listen now and visit Focuslinks.in for more ophthalmology episodes and resources.

episodes.title: HLA-B27 & Acute Anterior Uveitis: The Eye-Immune Connection
episodes.description:
Ever woken up with a red, painful eye so sensitive to light that even a cloudy morning feels blinding? That experience could be acute anterior uveitis — and a tiny genetic marker called HLA-B27 might be at the center of it all.

In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down everything you need to know about acute anterior uveitis (AAU), the most common form of uveitis, and explore its powerful connection to the HLA-B27 gene. We explain what HLA proteins actually do in your body, why this specific genetic variant dramatically raises your risk of eye inflammation, and what researchers currently understand about the underlying immune mechanisms driving that inflammation.

But the story goes far beyond the eye. We unpack the family of systemic diseases linked to HLA-B27 — including ankylosing spondylitis, reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease — and explain why a single episode of uveitis could be your body's first signal that something bigger is happening beneath the surface. You will also learn about the characteristic recurrence patterns of HLA-B27 associated uveitis, the serious complications that can arise without prompt treatment, and the treatment approaches that help patients manage both the eye inflammation and the underlying systemic disease.

Whether you are a patient, a caregiver, or simply someone curious about how genetics and immunity shape our health, this episode offers clear, accessible answers to genuinely complex questions.

Do not ignore a red, painful eye. Listen now, and visit Focuslinks dot in for more episodes dedicated to keeping your vision and your overall health in sharp focus.

episodes.title: Granulomatous vs Nongranulomatous Uveitis: KP Morphology
episodes.description:
What if a single glance at the back of the cornea could tell you exactly what's inflaming your patient's eye? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down one of ophthalmology's most clinically powerful diagnostic tools: keratic precipitate morphology and what it reveals about granulomatous versus nongranulomatous uveitis.

We start with the basics, explaining what keratic precipitates actually are, how inflammatory cells settle onto the corneal endothelium, and why their appearance varies so dramatically depending on the type of uveitis. You'll learn to distinguish the fine, dusty KPs of nongranulomatous uveitis, linked to HLA-B27 conditions like ankylosing spondylitis, from the large, greasy mutton fat KPs that signal granulomatous disease in conditions like sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, and Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada syndrome.

We walk through real clinical scenarios that show exactly how KP morphology shifts your differential diagnosis and drives your entire workup, from the questions you ask to the lab tests you order. We also cover the unique stellate KP pattern seen in Fuchs uveitis syndrome, the significance of old pigmented KPs as historical clues, and why KP findings must always be interpreted alongside other anterior and posterior segment signs.

Whether you're a medical student building your ophthalmology foundation, a resident preparing for exams, or a clinician looking to sharpen your slit lamp skills, this episode delivers focused, high-yield clinical insight you can apply immediately.

Listen now and start reading KPs like a language. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and clinical learning resources.

episodes.title: Intermediate Uveitis: Snowballs, Snowbanks & Hidden Eye Inflammation
episodes.description:
What do snowballs and snowbanks have to do with your eyes? More than you might think. In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take a deep dive into intermediate uveitis, one of the most fascinating and underrecognized forms of eye inflammation affecting young adults today.

Intermediate uveitis sits in the middle of the eye, targeting the vitreous, pars plana, and peripheral retina. It is bilateral in roughly 80% of cases, often silent in its early stages, and capable of quietly stealing vision through cystoid macular edema before a patient even suspects something is wrong. We break down the iconic snowball and snowbank findings that define this condition, explain why they matter clinically, and walk through how ophthalmologists diagnose and grade disease severity using these hallmark signs.

We also explore the critical systemic connections every clinician should know, including the strong association between intermediate uveitis and multiple sclerosis, sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, and Lyme disease. You will learn why a young patient presenting with unexplained floaters and a quiet-looking eye deserves a thorough workup, and why an MRI of the brain may be part of that conversation.

From first-line corticosteroid therapy and periocular injections to immunosuppressive agents, biologics, and pars plana vitrectomy, we cover the full treatment landscape in a clear, clinically grounded way.

Whether you are a medical student, an ophthalmology resident, or a curious clinician looking to sharpen your uveitis knowledge, this episode delivers everything you need in one focused listen.

Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes, resources, and eye health content. Do not forget to share this episode with a colleague who would find it valuable.

episodes.title: Sarcoidosis & Uveitis: Unmasking the Great Eye Mimic
episodes.description:
Could a mysterious eye condition be hiding a life-changing systemic diagnosis? In this eye-opening episode of Focus Cast, we dive deep into sarcoidosis — the "great mimicker" — and explore how it masquerades as uveitis in ways that challenge even the most experienced clinicians.

Sarcoidosis is a systemic inflammatory disease that forms granulomas across multiple organs, including the eyes. When it targets the uvea, it can present as anterior, intermediate, posterior, or panuveitis, making it notoriously difficult to diagnose. We break down the classic clinical clues that should raise red flags — from mutton fat keratic precipitates and iris nodules to candle wax drippings along retinal vessels — and explain why recognizing these signs early can be vision-saving.

We also walk through the full diagnostic workup, including serum ACE levels, chest imaging for bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and the gold standard of non-caseating granulomas on biopsy. You will learn why distinguishing sarcoidosis from tuberculosis is critical, how treatment strategies range from topical steroids to biologic agents, and why the eye is sometimes the very first place sarcoidosis reveals itself.

Whether you are an ophthalmologist, optometrist, medical student, or a patient navigating a long diagnostic journey, this episode gives you the clinical clarity and systemic perspective you need to understand sarcoid uveitis fully.

Tune in, stay curious, and remember — the eye is a window to the entire body. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and resources on eye health and ophthalmology.
